partner_context.their_ambition: HSL runs public transport for the Helsinki region — metro, tram, rail, bus and the year-round public ferry to Suomenlinna — all on one ticket, and it has committed to making every mode emission-free by 2035. Its ambition on the water is zero-emission island connectivity that works through the Baltic winter, and links for the new waterfront districts the city is building.
partner_context.where_navier_fits: Navier is the foiling-electric upgrade to a public ferry network HSL already runs. The Suomenlinna crossing, the recreation islands, the growing Laajasalo waterfront and the regional coast — flown clear of the water: faster, near-silent, low-wake and zero-emission, on the same HSL ticket, from the piers that already exist.

hero.eyebrow: Authority proposal · Helsinki, Finland · Helsinki Region Transport (HSL)
hero.title: Navier × Helsinki Ferries — the archipelago, on foils
hero.subtitle: A zero-emission foiling layer on the Suomenlinna crossing, the island network and the new Laajasalo waterfront: faster, quieter, all-electric public transport across the Helsinki archipelago.
hero.what_we_do_together: HSL brings the ferry network, the piers and the public-transport mandate; Navier brings the foiling-electric fleet, captain training and certification path. Together we run the same archipelago — faster and zero-emission — delivering the emission-free ferry HSL has already committed to.

why_now: HSL has published the target: emission-free public transport by 2035, zero-emission operations by 2030 — inside a city aiming for carbon-neutrality by 2035 and a country with a legislated 2035 net-zero. The commitment is made; a foiling-electric fleet is how the ferry links get there, at speed and with almost no wake through a sensitive, recreation-heavy archipelago.
multimodal_fit: Navier slots into the HSL network at Market Square (Kauppatori), where the ferries meet the tram and metro. Commuters and visitors step from a single HSL ticket straight onto a foil to Suomenlinna, the islands, Laajasalo or the regional coast — conventional ferries keep the heaviest runs underneath.

differentiation.why_navier: The platform is purpose-built for this archipelago: 10x more efficient than a planing hull, low-wake (vital around protected islands and dense summer traffic), near-silent, zero-emission, and viable year-round. It delivers HSL's published emission-free-ferry commitment on the links where speed and wake have kept diesel in service.

proof_points.claim: HSL has committed to emission-free ferries.
proof_points.evidence: HSL: emission-free public transport by 2035; zero-emission own operations by 2030.

proof_points.claim: The Suomenlinna ferry is public transport, not tourism.
proof_points.evidence: The Market Square–Suomenlinna ferry runs year-round as part of the HSL network and ticket.

proof_points.claim: The city and nation back it.
proof_points.evidence: Carbon-neutral Helsinki 2035; Finland's legislated national net-zero by 2035 — among the world's most ambitious.
proof_points.source: City of Helsinki / Finnish Climate Act

proof_points.claim: The platform is proven in service.
proof_points.evidence: 10 vessels delivered, 4,000+ flight hours, 2025 production sold out.

objections.concern: Can it run through a Baltic winter?
objections.response: The Suomenlinna ferry runs year-round today; foiling-electric routing is planned around ice conditions, and the platform's efficiency and quiet suit the shoulder-season and protected-island links especially well.

objections.concern: Does it disturb the protected islands?
objections.response: The opposite — low wake and near-silent operation reduce disturbance to Vallisaari's and Pihlajasaari's protected habitats compared with today's diesel vessels.

objections.concern: Does this replace the ferries people rely on?
objections.response: No — it's a faster, cleaner layer above them on the same HSL ticket; conventional ferries keep the heaviest runs.

the_ask.navier_brings: The software-defined foiling-electric fleet, captain training, and the maintenance and certification path for Baltic year-round operation.
the_ask.partner_brings: The HSL ferry route map, the piers, the single-ticket integration, and the emission-free-by-2035 mandate.
the_ask.next_step: Identify the first HSL ferry link — most likely Market Square–Suomenlinna — for a foiling-electric public pilot on the HSL ticket.

close.body: HSL has already promised Helsinki an emission-free ferry. Navier is how it arrives soonest — a fast, quiet, zero-emission crossing to Suomenlinna, the islands and the new waterfront districts, all on the same public ticket, and gentle on one of the Baltic's most treasured archipelagos.
